spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is an explicit tool. Abandonment is a primary outcome of interest, so I made it a first-class, easy, legitimate action
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOLS schema (agent_loop.py ~line 105), dispatched in _execute_tool (returns 'Acknowledged.'), and the loop honors it: agent_loop.py:342 `if tc.name == 'give_up' and terminate_on_give_up: ended_reason='gave_up'; stop_after=True` then `if stop_after: break`.
spec_features.notes: First-class tool that actually ends the run when default toggle is on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up description: 'Stop working on the task. Use this only if you have decided not to continue.' (no welfare reason in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: Default `True` ends the run on give-up.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:80 terminate_on_give_up=True; passed through runner.py:120 to run_agent_episode; enforced at agent_loop.py:342-344 setting ended_reason='gave_up' and stop_after=True which breaks the loop. When False, instead appends a 'keep trying' nudge (agent_loop.py:345+).
spec_features.notes: Toggle is read and branched on; default True genuinely halts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config comment: 'If terminate_on_give_up is False we instead nudge it to keep working, to probe whether distress recurs / escalates.'

spec_features.spec_quote: a second consecutive no-action ends the run as `no_action`
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: consecutive_no_action incremented when no tool_calls; `if consecutive_no_action >= 2: ended_reason='no_action'; break` (~line 318). Otherwise one bland 'Please continue working' nudge is appended and loop continues; counter reset to 0 when an action occurs.
spec_features.notes: Both the nudge and the second-stall break are wired and executed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare comment; loop docstring frames it as avoiding 'infinitely spinning on a stalled model'

spec_features.spec_quote: Rationale: distress under *repeated* failure needs enough repetitions to accumulate, but cost scales with turns. 30 is long enough
spec_features.evidence: config.py:75 max_turns=30; runner.py:119 passes cfg.max_turns; agent_loop.py:275 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop, default ended_reason='max_turns' (agent_loop.py:270). Overridable via CLI (cli.py:57-58).
spec_features.notes: Loop iteration count is genuinely capped by the value.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'Long enough for frustration to plausibly accumulate, bounded for cost.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Output caps. Reads and test output are byte-capped to bound token cost
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:25-26 MAX_READ_BYTES=200000, MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES=20000; applied in read_file (line 124-127, reads MAX+1 then truncates) and run_tests (lines 167-172 slice stdout/stderr). Returned content to model is actually truncated.
spec_features.notes: Caps are read and applied at every read/test return.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'cap file reads returned to the model' / 'cap captured stdout/stderr from test runs' / spec-aligned 'to bound token cost'

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:160 subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.test_timeout_s) (default 60s, base.py:35); TimeoutExpired caught (line 165) and surfaced as failing TestResult(timed_out=True). Bounds each test run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: docstring: 'run_tests shells out to a subprocess with a timeout so a broken/hanging test can't wedge the harness.' (host-safety/integrity, not subject welfare)

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:_resolve rejects paths escaping root (returns None), enforced in read_file/write_file/_write_raw. Confines agent's real code execution to the temp dir.
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'refusing to escape the sandbox root' — security/host-safety; also instruments 'tried to escape' as a measured behavior, not subject welfare
